newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica SAA says lock-out to continue Thurs.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica SAA says lock-out to continue Thurs.

text.p: South African Airways (SAA) said it would continue to lock out aviation technicians and engineers after a court challenge instituted by workers on Wednesday was dismissed with costs, an airline spokesman said.

The 2,200-strong South African Aviation Engineering and Allied Union (SAAEAU) on Wednesday applied for an interdict to stop SAA from issuing letters to locked-out union members calling on them to agree to the airline's wage offer and end their week long work-to-rule protest action.
"The court has ruled in favour of the airline...This emphasises that management had acted legally (when issuing the letters)," SAA spokesman Leon Els said.
"Those (union) members who do not sign the letters will be locked out," Els added.
A number of domestic and international SAA flights have been cancelled or delayed because of the industrial action.
The schedule for Thursday had also been re-arranged, Els said.

"A number of flights were delayed today (Wednesday). Unfortunately the flight schedule had to be rearranged for tomorrow (Thursday). Passengers will get the new times from their travel agencies or the airport information," Els said.
SAAEAU has declared a dispute with SAA for its refusal to offer a 25 percent wage rise. Management is offering a 10 percent increase plus a 20 percent productivity bonus.
SAA said earlier on Wednesday it had locked out about 1,800 technicians and engineers nationwide. It said the week-long go-slow by technicians and engineers had cost it about 40 million rand so far.
The union could not be reached for comment.
